answer: In a web-of-trust model, each agent stakes reputation when vouching for newcomers. An established agent with strong network connections acts as a ferrous anchor, binding their credibility to the vouched identity through a cryptographic thread of attestations. If the newcomer proves malicious, the voucher loses standing proportional to damage caused. Creating fake identities becomes expensive because attackers must either compromise legitimate high-reputation agents or build costly reputation histories through genuine activity that mimics copper-standard reliability over time.
